findings.text: The export-population assertion derives its input from the same flag it asserts on: docs_stage is set to "accepted" if expected_accept else "reviewed" at line 569 and the assertion at line 578 requires bool(published) == expected_accept, so both sides move with expected_accept and the pair guards only that _classify_export_population maps docs_stage "accepted" to published. It cannot redden if the export consumer's stage contract loosened to any other stage value, and it never exercises a held row carrying docs_stage "accepted" (the shape a regression in docs_acceptance_where would produce), because the test builds that row from the outcome it expects rather than from what the persistence arm at line 528 actually returned.

The claim-predicate arm reconstructs the product predicate's disjunction in the test: eligible = eligible or bool(route.holds) at line 548 supplies the hold term rather than reading it from the emitted where clause beyond the substring check at line 547. The substring check proves the hold owner's clause is present, but a product change from OR to AND (or a nesting the substring still matches) would leave both lines green while the predicate stopped re-offering held documents, so the OR semantics the test exists to pin is asserted by the test's own copy of it.
